name: tech
overview: The technology sector comprises software, semiconductor, and hardware enterprises characterized by high operating leverage, rapid innovation cycles, and substantial R&D investments.
tailwinds: Accelerating enterprise AI adoption, generative AI infrastructure buildout, public cloud migration, and pervasive digital transformation across traditional industries.
headwinds: Heightened regulatory scrutiny on big tech dominance, antitrust enforcement, export controls on cutting-edge semiconductors, and extended enterprise software procurement cycles.

name: retail
overview: The retail sector encompasses omnichannel superstores, e-commerce marketplaces, warehouse clubs, and specialty retailers driven by consumer discretionary spending, price elasticity, and supply chain execution.
tailwinds: Omnichannel fulfillment efficiency, retail media network high-margin advertising revenue, digital loyalty programs, and resilient consumer staples demand.
headwinds: Persistent wage inflation, shrink and inventory theft, discretionary spending pullback among lower-income demographics, and freight/logistics cost volatility.

name: logistics
overview: The logistics and freight transportation sector includes parcel express, freight forwarding, contract warehousing, truckload, and less-than-truckload (LTL) carriers sensitive to global trade volumes and industrial production cycles.
tailwinds: E-commerce parcel volume expansion, supply chain nearshoring/reshoring to North America, automated warehouse productivity gains, and carrier capacity discipline.
headwinds: Freight rate downcycles, excess carrier capacity following pandemic peaks, fuel price volatility, unionized labor wage pressures, and cyclical destocking.
